deqPrimaryOriginal.documentTitle: United States Antimony Corporation Thompson Falls Facility: Montana Air Quality Permit #2973-05
deqPrimaryOriginal.facilityLocation: Section 29, Township 21 North, Range 31 West, Sanders County, Montana

locators.finding: DEQ explicitly declares MAQP 2973-05 final and effective December 23 2025, not an actual furnace operation certificate.
DEQ specifies newly permitted five reduction, two remelt and two oxidizer furnaces, new baghouse equipment, and six previously permitted furnaces.
Initial EPA method source testing required in relation to initial startup of all new furnaces, within the specified post-startup time window; permit contains no executed test result.
Calendar-year production information must be supplied to DEQ in annual emissions inventory requests; no 2026 measured production figure is given.
Analysis summarizes nine newly permitted 3.0 MMBtu/hour furnaces plus six existing 0.85 MMBtu/hour furnaces; engineering input rating, not realized metal tonnage.

locators.section: Permit Analysis I.E Response to Public Comments
locators.finding: Applicant corrected an earlier mix-up in ratings and counts, and DEQ revised the permit text: all nine new furnace units have 3.0 MMBtu/hour ratings.

unresolvedEquipmentDiscrepancy.editorialStop: Do not quietly equate six permitted legacy furnaces in December 2025 with the reporter's seven older-building furnaces in August 2026. Request exact equipment lists and status/permit amendments; do not assert permit noncompliance.

originalRecordFollowUp.targetAgency: Montana DEQ Air Quality Field Services / Records
requestTargets: Any received initial source-test protocols, completed test reports, or compliance certification under permit Section II.B.1 for the nine new furnaces.
Any facility inspection notes, regulator field observations, or inspection reports distinguishing old and new furnace equipment from May through October 16, 2026.

Any DEQ-held, dated correspondence documenting actual operation of newly permitted furnace units; separately, any notices of qualifying de minimis changes under Section II.C.2 and permit amendments after December 2025. Section II.C.2 is not an unconditional furnace-startup notice requirement.
Any readily available calendar-year production or emissions inventory information that identifies realized activity from the newly permitted furnace lines, if separately maintained.
originalRecordFollowUp.materialStillAbsent: No regulatory post-startup report or inspection was located in the publicly surfaced DEQ permit/document listings as of October 16 2026. This does not prove it does not exist.
